title: Conjecture 1.2 (Lefmann, Rödl, Thomas)
statement_text: For all positive integers $l$ and $k$, $f(l, k) = l^{k-1}$.
context_text: Lefmann, Rödl, and Thomas conjectured in 1992 that the lower bound $f(l,k) \geq l^{k-1}$, established by a lexicographic labelling construction on $\{1,\ldots,l\}^{k-1}$, is tight in general. They proved the conjecture for $l \leq 2$ or $k \leq 4$ and for $l \geq (3k)^{2k}$.
paper_contribution: Proves the conjecture for $l \geq C_\varepsilon k^3 (\log k)^{1+\varepsilon}$ (Theorem 1.3) and establishes the general upper bound $f(l,k) \leq D_\varepsilon k(\log k)^{1+\varepsilon} \cdot l^{k-1}$ (Theorem 1.5), reducing the gap from exponential to polynomial in $k$.

title: Conjecture 1.7
statement_text: For all positive integers $l$ and $k$, $t(l, k) = l^{k-1}$.
context_text: A tournament is an orientation of a complete graph, and a directed walk is a sequence of vertices $x_0,\dots,x_l$ with $x_{i-1}x_i$ a directed edge for each $i$ (vertices and edges may repeat). Given a colouring $c$ of the edges, an $l$-flash is a directed walk $x_0,\dots,x_l$ with $c(x_0x_1),\dots,c(x_{l-1}x_l)$ all equal, and a $k$-rainbow is a directed walk $y_0,\dots,y_k$ with $c(y_0y_1),\dots,c(y_{k-1}y_k)$ all distinct (any number of colours may be used). $t(l,k)$ is the smallest integer such that every edge colouring of any tournament with more than $t(l,k)$ vertices contains an $l$-flash or a $k$-rainbow, and $f(l,k)$ is the same quantity restricted to transitive tournaments (i.e. to colourings of the pairs of $[n]$, with walks along increasing vertices). Lefmann, Rödl and Thomas showed $f(l,k)\ge l^{k-1}$ (label vertices by strings of $\{1,\dots,l\}^{k-1}$ in lexicographic order and colour $uv$, $u<v$, by an index where $u$ is smaller than $v$) and conjectured $f(l,k)=l^{k-1}$; they proved it for $l\le2$ or $k\le4$ or $l\ge(3k)^{2k}$, and the authors prove it for $l\ge k^3(\log k)^{1+o(1)}$. Since $t(l,k)\ge f(l,k)\ge l^{k-1}$, this conjecture is a tournament strengthening of theirs. The authors prove $t(l,k)\le(1+2/\sqrt{l})^k l^{k-1}$, which confirms it asymptotically for $l=\omega(k^2)$, and $t(l,k)\le D_\varepsilon k(\log k)^{1+\varepsilon}l^{k-1}$; they also show that for $l\ge2$, $k\ge3$ some tournament with $f(l,k)-1$ vertices has no good colouring, so transitive tournaments are not the worst. They note the conjecture remains wide open for every $l\ge2$, $k\ge3$, and that the case $l=2$ together with their results would give it for $l\ge k^3(\log k)^{1+o(1)}$.
